newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish currency seen unaffected by French poll.
newsitem.headline: Danish currency seen unaffected by French poll.

text.p: Danish analysts on Monday saw little short-term effect on the crown likely to result from Sunday's election win for the French left but said it could have benefits for bond prices.

"We think we will continue to see a very steady Danish crown against the mark, we don't really think the French elections should have any impact on the relationship between the mark and the crown," Jyske Bank's Klaus Nielsen told Reuters.

"Of course if we see very negative bond markets in Europe, if we see yields going much higher in Spain, Italy, Portugal Sweden and so on, then maybe we could have a spillover effect from the bond market to the currency, but otherwise I think it would be rather limited," he added.
Key Danish government bond prices slipped slightly on Monday morning but the crown was virtually unchanged at around 3.8082 to the mark.

At 0930 GMT the benchmark eight percent bond due in 2006 was down 0.02 point compared to Friday's close, trading at 110.36 with a yield of 6.41 percent. The seven percent 2007, due to become the benchmark later this year, was 0.13 point down at 102.88, yielding 6.60 percent.

Unibank Markets' Klaus Dalsgaard said that the French Socialists' policies in favour of wide membership of Economic and Monetary Union and more flexible entrance requirements could reduce the yield gap between the Danish and German benchmark bonds, currently about 66 basis points for the 2007 paper.
"The price of staying out will be significantly lower with a broader EMU," Dalsgaard said.
"I think that Denmark will do well compared to both Germany and France but I can also easily imagine that money will go to other markets, such as Britain and the United States," he added.
Denmark fulfils the economic criteria for EMU membership but its citizens voted to stay out, in a binding 1993 referendum.
